welcome.title: Welcome, Explorer!
welcome.pari_tip: There are no wrong ideas in this workbook. Try your best, ask questions, and have fun learning about AI!

syllabus.objective: I can explain the difference between following rules and
I can collect data and show it in a table and pictograph.
I can label examples and explain training and testing.
I can use and build a decision tree.
I can use loops to make algorithms shorter.
I can write a simple chatbot script.
I can spot when AI might be wrong or unfair.

units.title: Rules or Learning?
learn_paragraphs:
Some machines follow fixed rules: IF the button is pressed, THEN the light
turns on.
AI can learn from examples instead of only following rules. A music app
learns which songs you like.
Rules are good for simple jobs. Learning helps with jobs that have too many
cases to write rules for.

new_words.definition: when AI favours some things because of its examples
one path in a decision tree

units.did_you_know: A computer called Deep Blue beat the world chess champion in a match in 1997.
units.think_and_talk: Why can't we write rules for everything a robot might see?

units.title: Data is Everywhere
learn_paragraphs:
Data is information: numbers, words, pictures and sounds.
AI needs data to learn. The more good data it has, the better it can learn.
We can collect data with a survey and count it with tally marks: |||| for
five.
units.did_you_know: Every photo you take is data made of tiny coloured dots.
units.think_and_talk: What other data could you collect about your class?
units.self_check: I can collect data and show it in a table and pictograph.

units.title: Teaching a Machine
learn_paragraphs:
To teach AI, we show it many examples with labels, like pictures marked
“cat” or “dog”. This is called training.
Different examples help: big, small, light and dark cats.
Then we test the AI with new pictures it has never seen.

new_words.definition: a name we give to an example

units.did_you_know: Image AIs are often trained on thousands or even millions of pictures.
units.think_and_talk: What might happen if we trained an AI with only 3 pictures?
units.self_check: I can label examples and explain training and testing.

units.title: Decision Trees
learn_paragraphs:
A decision tree asks yes or no questions to reach an answer.
Each answer takes you down a different branch, like a path in a forest.
AI can use decision trees to make choices step by step.

new_words.definition: to get better by seeing examples

units.did_you_know: Decision trees are also used to help with choices in hospitals and banks.
units.think_and_talk: How many questions do you need to guess one of 8 animals?
units.self_check: I can use and build a decision tree.

units.title: Algorithms and Loops
learn_paragraphs:
A sequence is steps in order. A loop repeats steps.
Instead of writing “clap” five times, we write: repeat 5 times: clap.
Loops make algorithms shorter and easier to read.

new_words.definition: saying yes before something is done
what we ask to find out

units.did_you_know: Video games use loops to keep checking which buttons you press.
units.think_and_talk: What shape does “repeat 4 times: draw line, turn right” make?
units.self_check: I can use loops to make algorithms shorter.

units.title: Chatbots
learn_paragraphs:
A chatbot is a computer program that chats with people.
Simple chatbots follow a script: if the user says this, reply with that.
Smarter chatbots use AI to understand many different ways of saying the
same thing.

new_words.definition: treating people and their work well
an exact instruction: IF this, THEN that

units.did_you_know: One of the first chatbots, ELIZA, was made in the 1960s.
units.think_and_talk: Why do chatbots need to understand different ways of asking?
units.self_check: I can write a simple chatbot script.

units.title: When AI Gets It Wrong
learn_paragraphs:
AI only knows what it learned from its examples. If it saw only black cats, it
may not know an orange cat is a cat.
When examples leave things out, AI can be unfair. This is called bias.
People must check AI for mistakes and give it fair, varied examples.

new_words.definition: asking people questions to collect data

units.did_you_know: AI can sound very sure and still be wrong, so always double-check.
units.think_and_talk: Who should check if an AI is fair?
units.self_check: I can spot when AI might be wrong or unfair.

units.title: Digital Citizen
learn_paragraphs:
A good digital citizen is safe, kind and honest online.
Use strong passwords, think before you share, and ask permission before
using someone's photo.
Respect other people's work, and tell a trusted adult if something feels
wrong.
units.did_you_know: Two-step verification adds a second lock to an online account.
units.think_and_talk: Is it okay to copy a friend's drawing and post it online? Why?
units.self_check: I can be safe, kind and respectful online.
